transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I guess… I’ve just been feeling really restless. Like I’m wound too tight and can’t quite settle down, even when I’m supposed to be sitting calmly in a meeting, or painting, or doing yoga.
Do you have any recurring thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?
Not really… I mean, not in a way I’d call recurring thoughts. My mind can feel busy, but I haven’t noticed one particular thought getting stuck like that.
Do you often feel anxious?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get tense sometimes, like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I often feel anxious.
Do you ever feel like you have to repeat certain actions or behaviors?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I have little habits like anyone, but nothing I feel like I have to repeat.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or having trouble sitting still?

Yeah… I do. Mostly little things. Like on calls with suppliers, my foot will be bouncing under the desk, or I’ll be clicking a pen or twisting my ring. Sometimes I have to mute myself or keep my hands out of view.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Sometimes, yes. Not in huge ways, but… in vendor negotiations, or when I’m mentoring students, I’ll jump in with an answer before they’ve finished the question. Then I realize I missed some qualifier or detail they were getting to.
Have you noticed your impulsivity affecting your relationships with others?

A little, yes. Mostly people just get frustrated with me. At home, dinners can get tense because I jump in or talk over someone without meaning to.

At work it’s happened too… I’ve rushed and then a purchase order needed correcting, so my planning coordinator has had to look over things more closely.
Do you often have trouble paying attention to details or making careless mistakes?

Yes… sometimes. I’ll think I’ve gone through a vendor spreadsheet carefully, and then our planning coordinator will catch something I missed — like a SKU flipped around, a freight surcharge I didn’t include, or the wrong quantity carried into the purchase order. It’s not constant, but it has happened enough the last couple years that I notice it.
Do you feel like your restlessness and impulsivity are causing problems in your daily life?

Yes… somewhat. It’s not ruining everything, but it does cause problems. At work, I’ve had purchase orders that needed correcting, and my planning coordinator ends up reviewing things more closely. And at home, dinners can get tense because people feel like I’m talking over them.
When did you first notice these feelings of restlessness and impulsivity?
Pretty early, I think. I remember in elementary school getting notes sent home because I’d pop out of my seat, talk over other kids, or blurt out an answer before the teacher was even done asking.
Would you say these problems with restlessness and impulsivity have been mild, moderate, or severe?

I’d say mild. It’s there, but not… extreme. At work it’s meant some purchase orders had to be corrected, and my planning coordinator checks things more closely. At home, family dinners can get a little tense because people feel like I’m talking over them.
Have you experienced these feelings of restlessness and impulsivity consistently throughout your life?

Not exactly consistently, no. It’s been around in some way, but it’s been harder to manage for… about two years now. Maybe a little over—since the conflicts with my in-laws started taking up more of our evenings.
Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty sustaining focus during tasks?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I can usually focus if I have to. I haven’t noticed that being the main problem, I guess.
Have you experienced significant symptoms of hyperactivity?
Yes… I think so. It’s mostly this restless feeling, like I’m wound too tight. Even when I’m supposed to be sitting calmly in a meeting, or painting, or doing yoga, I can’t really fully settle.
Do you often have trouble following through on instructions or finishing tasks?
I don’t think that’s a big issue for me. I mean, I might put things off sometimes, but not… not in a way I’ve really thought of as a problem.
Did you have trouble paying attention or following instructions when you were a kid?

A little, maybe. I remember in elementary school there were notes sent home… mostly because I kept getting out of my seat, talking over other kids, or blurting out answers before the teacher finished asking. I don’t remember it as much as not understanding instructions, more that I was too quick or restless.
Did you often have trouble paying attention in class when you were a kid?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember it being a big thing, honestly. Maybe sometimes, but nothing specific comes to mind.
Have you ever lost a job, had a relationship end, or experienced other significant consequences because of your restlessness and impulsivity?

I haven’t lost a job or anything like that. But… it has caused some issues. At work, there have been purchase orders I had to correct, and my planning coordinator started checking things more closely. And at home, family dinners can get tense because people feel like I’m talking over them.
Have you experienced these feelings of restlessness and impulsivity in multiple areas of your life, such as at work, at home, and in social situations?

Yes… I think so. It’s not just one place. I get that wound-up feeling at work, like in planning meetings when I’m supposed to just sit and listen. And it can happen at home too, or even when I’m doing something that’s supposed to be relaxing, like painting or yoga. I just don’t fully settle.
